subject.title: Unbounded Promise.all file unlinks cause EMFILE/EBUSY crashes

question: Should Gateway agents.delete be hardened to sequential or tightly bounded trash operations now, despite current source not proving the reported thousands-file EMFILE/EBUSY path?
rationale: The source confirms concurrent trash calls, but the claimed unbounded scale is contradicted by the current attestation helper, so a human should decide whether preventive hardening is worthwhile without a concrete failing repro.

options.title: Harden deletion ordering now
options.body: Change Gateway agents.delete to await trash targets sequentially or through a tiny bounded helper, preserving existing semantics and adding regression coverage for ordering and shared-workspace retention.

options.title: Ask for concrete repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open until the reporter provides logs or a minimal workspace/config state that actually reaches EMFILE or EBUSY on current main.

options.title: Close as source-disproved
options.body: Close only if maintainers consider the bounded current target list sufficient to reject the reported failure mode.

recommendation.title: Harden deletion ordering now
recommendation.body: Change Gateway agents.delete to await trash targets sequentially or through a tiny bounded helper, preserving existing semantics and adding regression coverage for ordering and shared-workspace retention.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad ownership of agents delete docs, config mutation behavior, and cleanup semantics across Gateway and CLI paths.
